metas.name: Black and purple pole markings
metas.note: These black-and-purple pole markings are only found on poles in the Santo Domingo area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Mountains
metas.note:
If you have mountains to the North, you will always be in Santiago de los Caballeros.

NOTE: Although some parts of Santo Domingo are hilly, you will never see proper mountains like this one.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Santiago de los Caballeros street signs
metas.note:
Santiago de los Caballeros street signs are useally generic street signs with no ''ADN'' written on them and no shield icon on the side.

NOTE: These street signs can very rarely be found in Santo Domingo aswell.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic for more clues.

metas.name: Santo Domingo Este street signs
metas.note: Santo Domingo Este street signs have a distinct shield icon on the side of the name. Their mainly found in and around Alma Rosa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic for more clues.

metas.name: Santo Domingo Este Yellow pole markings
metas.note:
Yellow markings around poles are super common in Santo Domingo Este. Pole markings (useally yellow) with a name and TAXI with numbers written on them are unique to Santo Domingo Este and the region north of Santo Domingo.

Yellow pole markings can sometimes also be seen in Santo Domingo and rarely in Santiago de los Caballeros.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic for more clues.

metas.name: Santo Domingo outskirts
metas.note: This type of landscape is found on the outskirts of Santo Domingo. It is characterised by narrow dirt tracks, whitish dirt, dried green shrubbery and debris next to the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Santo Domingo street name signs
metas.note: Street name signs in Santo Domingo often contain the letters “ADN”, a reference to the Distrito Nacional, which the city is located in.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Santo Domingo vibes
metas.note: As the capital and largest city, Santo Domingo has a more developed downtown area, with tall buildings and wide avenues.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.

metas.name: Yellow traffic light poles
metas.note:
Yellow traffic light poles are typically found in the city of Santiago de los Caballeros.

NOTE: This only applies to traffic light poles - yellow signposts are common in both cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic.
